$(a)$: $20\text{ g}$ is $20 \times 1,000 = 20,000\text{ mg}$. $20,000$ is more than $200$, so $20\text{ g} > 200\text{ mg}$.
$(d)$: $9,000\text{ mg}$ is $9,000 \div 1,000 = 9\text{ g}$. $9\text{ g}$ is less than $90\text{ g}$, so $9,000\text{ mg} < 90\text{ g}$.

Check: in every part both weights were in the same unit before they were compared.

item.question: Add 3 kg 600 g and 2 kg 700 g in three ways. These are practice values.
steps: Way 1, in parts. Add the kilograms: 3 + 2 = 5 kg.
Add the grams: 600 + 700 = 1,300 g. 1,000 g is 1 kg, so 1,300 g is 1 kg 300 g.
Put the parts together: 5 kg + 1 kg 300 g = 6 kg 300 g.
Way 2, in a column. Add the g column: 600 + 700 = 1,300. Write 300 g and carry 1 kg.
Add the kg column: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 kg. The answer is 6 kg 300 g.
6,300 g is 6 kg 300 g. All three ways give the same weight.
item.text:
Worked example: Add 3 kg 600 g and 2 kg 700 g in three ways. These are practice values.
1. Way 1, in parts. Add the kilograms: 3 + 2 = 5 kg.
2. Add the grams: 600 + 700 = 1,300 g. 1,000 g is 1 kg, so 1,300 g is 1 kg 300 g.
3. Put the parts together: 5 kg + 1 kg 300 g = 6 kg 300 g.
4. Way 2, in a column. Add the g column: 600 + 700 = 1,300. Write 300 g and carry 1 kg.
5. Add the kg column: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 kg. The answer is 6 kg 300 g.
6. Way 3, in grams. 3 kg 600 g is 3,600 g and 2 kg 700 g is 2,700 g. 3,600 + 2,700 = 6,300 g.
7. 6,300 g is 6 kg 300 g. All three ways give the same weight.
Answer: 3 kg 600 g + 2 kg 700 g = 6 kg 300 g

item.question: Subtract 2 kg 800 g from 5 kg 200 g in three ways. These are practice values.
steps: Way 1, take away in parts. 5 kg 200 g − 200 g leaves 5 kg.
Still to take away: 800 − 200 = 600 g. 3 kg is 3,000 g and 3,000 − 600 = 2,400 g, which is 2 kg 400 g.
Way 2, in a column. 200 g is fewer than 800 g, so break 1 kg into 1,000 g. 5 kg 200 g becomes 4 kg 1,200 g.
1,200 − 800 = 400 g and 4 − 2 = 2 kg. The answer is 2 kg 400 g.
2,400 g is 2 kg 400 g. All three ways give the same weight.
item.text:
Worked example: Subtract 2 kg 800 g from 5 kg 200 g in three ways. These are practice values.
1. Way 1, take away in parts. 5 kg 200 g − 200 g leaves 5 kg.
2. 5 kg − 2 kg leaves 3 kg.
3. Still to take away: 800 − 200 = 600 g. 3 kg is 3,000 g and 3,000 − 600 = 2,400 g, which is 2 kg 400 g.
4. Way 2, in a column. 200 g is fewer than 800 g, so break 1 kg into 1,000 g. 5 kg 200 g becomes 4 kg 1,200 g.
5. 1,200 − 800 = 400 g and 4 − 2 = 2 kg. The answer is 2 kg 400 g.
6. Way 3, in grams. 5 kg 200 g is 5,200 g and 2 kg 800 g is 2,800 g. 5,200 − 2,800 = 2,400 g.
7. 2,400 g is 2 kg 400 g. All three ways give the same weight.
Answer: 5 kg 200 g − 2 kg 800 g = 2 kg 400 g
